methodology: Performance baseline for the ghostty reference oracle on Apple M4 Pro (arm64), captured in isolation (no other heavy work concurrent). BENCHMARKS: the build stage produced a single multiplexed `ghostty-bench` runner (NOT separate ghostty-bench-* binaries); it dispatches by a `+<action>` subcommand (actions: terminal-parser, terminal-stream, codepoint-width, grapheme-break, is-symbol, osc-parser, screen-clone). Each action reads a `--data <file>` corpus, runs its step EXACTLY ONCE (Benchmark.RunMode .once), and PRINTS NOTHING (the internal RunResult is discarded). The only measurable signal is therefore the end-to-end process wall-clock, which we measure with time.monotonic() deltas around subprocess.run INSIDE one Python process (run_benchmarks.py). [A first bash attempt that spawned a separate `python -c time.monotonic()` for the start and end timestamps produced garbage/negative durations because monotonic clocks are not comparable across processes; that data was discarded and the harness rewritten.] Corpora were pre-generated once with `ghostty-gen` (deterministic seed=42 for utf8) and truncated to fixed sizes (64 MiB for data-throughput benches; 256 KiB for screen-clone). Per AGENTS.md, generation is NOT piped into benchmarking. stderr is discarded (terminal stream/parser emit per-byte warn logs on control bytes; we use clean printable ASCII for the stream benches and utf8 for the unicode benches). Each config: 1 warmup (discarded) + N timed reps; median reported (also min/max and all reps). OPTIMIZE MODE: the build stage built bench binaries with default optimize = DEBUG (`zig build -Demit-bench=true`, no -Doptimize). AGENTS.md explicitly warns Debug benchmarks are 'very slow and not representative'. We therefore report BOTH: (a) ReleaseFast (N=7) as the REPRESENTATIVE HEADLINE baseline, built isolated under phase-0 with `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Demit-macos-app=false` (ghostty tree untouched), and (b) Debug (N=5) as the literal as-built-in-build-stage numbers. Use ReleaseFast for any parity/perf comparison; Debug is recorded for completeness only. STARTUP: the main GUI `ghostty` binary was NOT built in the build stage, so `ghostty +version` cannot be timed here (documented TODO). The available proxy is the no-arg `ghostty-bench` invocation (process spawn + Zig runtime init + arg parse + immediate NoAction exit), median of 15 runs after 3 warmups; this is dominated by macOS process-spawn overhead and should not be read as terminal GUI startup. hyperfine is NOT installed on this machine; the Python harness substitutes for it.

binary_sizes_bytes._rule: Re-based 2026-10-10 by P8-W10 PERF to the oracle at the pin 246f70287 (artifacts rebuilt by P8-W10 T0), following P7-W22 (V16, N512), which set the method at 12752b2ac: built ReleaseFast (`zig build -Demit-lib-vt=true -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` for the two libraries; the perf README recipe for ghostty-bench/ghostty-gen) and preserved in ~/rustty-oracle-artifacts/<name>-246f70287. Each label names the Rustty artifact that plays the same role (`rustty_counterpart`, a path under the repo root, built with `rustty_build`) and carries its own `tolerance` (a fraction; G8 falls back to 0 for a label without one). tolerance = max(0, ceil(measured_gap_percent + 2)) / 100, where measured_gap is (rustty_bytes - bytes) / bytes measured at the re-base; the 2 points are headroom for toolchain/codegen jitter, the gap itself is itemized in `gap_attribution`. The labels the retired 4749c4e93 series carried with no Rustty counterpart, and the static `libghostty-vt.a` (an unpruned Rust staticlib is not like-for-like; the dylib is its linked size), are in `binary_sizes_dropped` with the reason. Like the timing axis, this is an oracle-parity fence, not a self-regression fence.

ghostty-bench (ReleaseFast).gap_attribution: Rustty is 0.728x (-27.2%) at 246f70287 (0.734x, -26.6% at 12752b2ac); no growth past the oracle is allowed.

ghostty-gen (ReleaseFast).gap_attribution: +8.7% (+40,568 B) at 246f70287 (+8.8%, +40,888 B at 12752b2ac, itemized there by P7-W22): __TEXT +22 KB is unwind data (__eh_frame 33.0 vs 20.8 KB, __gcc_except_tab 5.6 KB, __unwind_info +3.3 KB; `release-fast` keeps panic=unwind for the bench's codegen, N512) with __text itself 8 KB smaller than the oracle's; __LINKEDIT +33 KB is the symbol table of Rust's longer mangled names.

libghostty-vt.0.1.0.dylib (shared).gap_attribution: +7.2% (+142,240 B) at 246f70287 (+7.6%, +146,976 B at 12752b2ac, after N512 took it from 2,498,112 B (1.30x); itemized there by P7-W22): __text 1,270 KB vs 1,081 KB. Itemized: `overflow-checks = true` (DG2, the release profile's ReleaseSafe trap parity) 55 KB; std's panic/backtrace runtime, linked by std's default panic hook even though panic.rs replaces it at run time (gimli 29 KB, rustc_demangle 19 KB, addr2line 11 KB, object 3 KB of __text, plus their std glue; removable only with nightly build-std); the grapheme precompute table is 16 KB (2-byte Value) against the oracle's 8 KB; the rest is codegen.

binary_sizes_dropped._rule: Labels of the retired 4749c4e93 series with no Rustty counterpart at the pin, dropped from the fence by P7-W22 (V16), and the pin's `libghostty-vt.a (static)`, dropped by the P7-W22 review (its reason below). Values kept for the record.

libghostty-vt.a (static).gap_attribution: +143.7%: a Rust staticlib archives the Rust toolchain's rlibs and every dependency's objects whole, unpruned (std 8.4 MB, compiler_builtins 2.8 MB, core 2.4 MB, alloc 0.6 MB, objc2_foundation 4.0 MB, almost none of which reaches the linked dylib); a consumer's final link dead-strips them, and the linked size of the same code is the dylib label. The fence still catches a newly bundled dependency or growth past +2 points.
libghostty-vt.a (static).dropped_reason: dropped by the P7-W22 review: a Rust staticlib archives the toolchain's rlibs and every dependency's objects whole and unpruned (std, compiler_builtins, core, alloc, objc2_foundation), so the +143.7% gap is archive packaging, not code, and its 146% tolerance would fence almost nothing. The linked size of the same code is the `libghostty-vt.0.1.0.dylib (shared)` label, which is the real size fence; `cargo build -p rustty-vt-c --release` still builds the .a, it is just not measured.

benchmarks_rule: Re-based 2026-10-10 by P8-W10 PERF to the oracle at the pin 246f70287: ~/rustty-oracle-artifacts/ghostty-bench-246f70287 (sha256 37c6317668c020e6be5b62ca2e4d2d45c9afee41ff9e60d2920c4171490fee49, built ReleaseFast with Zig 0.16.0 by P8-W10 T0), measured with `run_benchmarks.py <oracle> <out.jsonl> 7` on the idle host (1-minute load 1.44 at the start, 1.29 at the end; both VMs stopped, no build running; Apple M4 Pro, macOS 26.5.1) over the same four corpora. Same method as the P7-W23 (V17) re-base at 12752b2ac, which it replaces. One row per id, ReleaseFast only: there is no Debug oracle bench at the pin, so the 14 Debug rows of the retired series are in `benchmarks_dropped_debug`, and the retired 4749c4e93 ReleaseFast rows are kept for the record in `benchmarks_retired_4749c4e93`. G8 compares only `benchmarks`. The screen-clone `metric` string is prose kept byte-identical to ws10_suite.py's emitted rows (G8 joins on median_s); at the pin stepRender runs 50_000 iterations on both sides.

reproduce.host_metadata: sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string hw.model hw.ncpu hw.memsize; sw_vers; uname -mrs; zig version
reproduce.generate_corpora: ghostty-gen +utf8 --seed=42  > utf8.full   (cap to 64 MiB via head -c 67108864); ghostty-gen +ascii          > ascii.full  (cap 64 MiB); ghostty-gen +osc --style=parser --p-valid=0.5 > osc-parser.full (cap 64 MiB); head -c 262144 ascii.bin > ascii-small.bin. NOTE: ghostty-gen streams forever; run it to a file in the background and KILL it once the file exceeds the target, then head -c to the exact size. Action names REQUIRE a leading '+'.
reproduce.per_benchmark: each benchmarks[].cmd is the exact command; throughput = corpus_bytes / median_s; screen-clone metric = 1000 / median_s clones/s.
